audit.whatIsWrong: Gnar's dash is attributed to W in four places: whys[1] "his short W hop", whys[2] "the W hop escape he was missing", whys[3] "he can direct his W hop to dodge mushrooms", early "His W hop is short and directional".
audit.why: Hop / Crunch is E. W is Hyper (mini, a stacking on-attack damage-and-speed passive) / Wallop (Mega, an area stun). Getting the slot wrong is not cosmetic here: the entry tells the player to trade around 'his W', which in mini form is a passive that is always available, while the actual thing to bait — the 22-second Hop — goes untracked.
audit.corrected: Hop / Crunch is E, 475 range, 22 seconds at rank 1. W is Hyper in mini form and the Wallop stun in Mega form.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gnar.json (E Hop/Crunch: dash, range 475, cooldown 22/19.5/17/14.5/12; W Hyper/Wallop: 'Gnar's attacks and spells hype him up' / 'smash down on the area in front of him, stunning enemies')

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says "At Level 6 he gains the ability to Mega-transform at any point" and whys[4] says "Level 6 lets him choose when to transform".
audit.why: Mega Gnar is gated by Rage, not by level — Rage Gene transforms him whenever the bar fills, which happens in the first few levels of any traded lane. What level 6 actually unlocks is GNAR!, the Mega-only ultimate. A Teemo who believes Mega Gnar cannot appear before 6 will take a level 3-5 trade against a champion who has just doubled his stats.
audit.corrected: Rage decides the transformation from level 1; level 6 only adds GNAR! on top. Watch the bar, not the level.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gnar.json (P Rage Gene: 'While in combat Gnar generates Rage. At maximum Rage his next ability will transform him into Mega Gnar' — no level condition; R GNAR!: Mega-only)

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number appears anywhere in either layer, and the full layer names GNAR! as the cooldown to track even in the Level 2 phase, where it does not exist yet.
audit.why: The lane-deciding cooldowns are Hop at 22/19.5/17/14.5/12 and Boomerang Throw at 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 — both enormous next to Blinding Dart's flat 7 seconds. Boomerang Throw's cooldown is also reduced when Gnar catches the returning boomerang, which is exactly why the entry's 'walk toward him so he cannot catch the return' advice matters, and quantifying it turns a habit into a decision. GNAR! is 90 seconds at rank 1 and only relevant from level 6.
audit.corrected: Hop 22s at rank 1; Boomerang Throw 16s at rank 1 and shorter if he catches it; GNAR! 90s at rank 1. Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank, so you get two to three blinds per Hop.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gnar.json (E 22/19.5/17/14.5/12; Q 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, 'If he catches the boomerang its cooldown is reduced'; R 90/60/30)

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] and spikes[0].text write "Blinding Shot"; whys[1] also reads "Blinding Shot erase his auto window" (subject-verb disagreement); wants.foe[2] writes "your Blinding Shot".

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] and spikes[2].text call the item "Liandry's Angueur".
audit.why: No such item; the Teemo full layer writes it as Liandry's Torment.

_missing-interactions.json emits 'knockup-enabler: Both sides carry displacement (Noxious Trap (R) vs GNAR! (R))' for this matchup. The Gnar half is right — GNAR! knocks up and stuns against terrain — but the Teemo half is a false positive: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json derives a 'knockup' flag on Noxious Trap that the ability does not have. Mushrooms slow and damage; they do not displace. I wrote nothing for this rule.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (R Noxious Trap description: 'releases a poisonous cloud, slowing enemies and damaging them over time' — no displacement, despite the derived knockup flag)

audit.why: The entry's core early-game instruction — throw Blinding Dart as the boomerang leaves his hand so the blind lands on the return attempt, and walk at him to deny the catch — is genuinely good and mechanically sound. I kept it and only added the cooldown consequence of denying the catch.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gnar.json (Q: 'If he catches the boomerang its cooldown is reduced')

edits.before: Mini-Gnar is a ranged auto-trader with a boomerang that has to travel back to him — the moment he throws Boomerang Throw, walk toward him so he cannot catch the return, force a trade, and let your E poison tick while he stands there autoless. Blinding Shot pre-emptively erases his auto window: throw Q the instant his boomerang leaves his hand so the blind lands on the return attempt. His W hop is short and directional — it does not let him chase you, so a W-boosted Move Quick retreat beats it clean. Keep the wave on your side of the river and do NOT stack his GNAR! meter by letting him take free chip shots — each auto he lands accelerates rage.
edits.after: Mini-Gnar is a ranged auto-trader with a boomerang that has to travel back to him — the moment he throws Boomerang Throw, walk toward him so he cannot catch the return, force a trade, and let your E poison tick while he stands there autoless. Denying the catch is worth real seconds: the throw is 16s at rank 1 and catching it cuts that down. Blinding Dart pre-emptively erases his auto window: throw Q the instant the boomerang leaves his hand so the blind lands on the return attempt. Hop (E) is 22 seconds at rank 1, so once he spends it a Move Quick retreat beats him clean. Keep the wave on your side and do NOT feed his rage bar with free chip shots.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 is where the lane gets honest. Mini-Gnar's poke is real and he can now kite your mushrooms with his hop, so shroom placement matters: put them at the lane bushes and the path he uses to catch the boomerang return, not in a straight line he reads. At Level 6 he gains the ability to Mega-transform at any point — watch his rage bar. If he transforms near a wall, treat it like a Malphite ultimate: he WILL try to GNAR! wall-slam you. Your answer is mushrooms on every wall approach and Move Quick the moment you see the purple glow. Never take a trade when his bar is above roughly 60% — let him rage-decay back to mini before you engage again.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 is where the lane gets honest. Mini-Gnar poke is real and Hop (E) lets him kite your mushrooms, so shroom placement matters: put them at the lane bushes and the path he uses to catch the boomerang return, not in a straight line he reads. He can already turn Mega at any level — Rage does that, not a level — but at 6 he adds GNAR!, and if he transforms near a wall he WILL try to wall-slam you. Your answer is mushrooms on every wall approach and Move Quick the moment you see the purple glow. Never take a trade when his bar is above roughly 60% — let him rage-decay back to mini before you engage again.

notes: The full layer's focus block for this matchup is focus.text 'Gnar GNAR!' / letters ['R'], which points the player at an ability that does not exist until level 6 and is Mega-only. Hop/Crunch (E) is the cooldown that actually governs every lane decision. I did not propose an edit to focus because it is not on the writable-path list as a sub-path, but somebody with write access to that field should reconsider it. I also left the level chart alone: 55.17% is a comfortable Teemo win rate against a Teemo 2 / Skill 3 / Gnar 2 chart, which under-sells him a little, but the Gnar-favoured stages (level 6 and two items) are genuinely his and I had no mechanical basis for shifting a specific stage.
